boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Princeton University Library settings spanning silent reading rooms, flexible individual seating, and reservable collaborative spaces.

cards.title: Dulles Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Firestone Library · first floor
cards.notes: Set up at one of the open tables for quiet individual work; this is a silent room beside the Thomas-Graham Reading Room.
cards.short_summary: A high-ceilinged silent reading room for focused solo sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library describes Dulles as a silent, high-ceilinged, open study space on Firestone's first floor.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Firestone Library; confirm current building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Elfers Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Firestone Library · third floor
cards.notes: Use this third-floor open room when you need a silent setting; bring the materials you plan to work through.
cards.short_summary: A large silent study room on Firestone’s third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library identifies Elfers as a large, high-ceilinged, silent, open study space on Firestone's third floor.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Firestone Library; confirm current building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Trustee Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Firestone Library · first floor
cards.notes: Choose a seat in this first-floor room for silent work, especially when your task benefits from a large shared reading hall.
cards.short_summary: A large, high-ceilinged silent study space in Firestone.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library calls the Trustee Reading Room a large, high-ceilinged, silent study space on Firestone's first floor.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Firestone Library; confirm current building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Scribner Solarium
cards.subtitle: Firestone Library · first floor
cards.notes: Bring reading or laptop work to this quiet, open room; its natural light is the documented physical feature to look for.
cards.short_summary: A quiet Firestone reading room filled with natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library describes the Scribner Solarium as a quiet, open reading room filled with natural light.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Firestone Library; confirm current building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Tower Reading Rooms
cards.subtitle: Firestone Library tower
cards.notes: Head to the tower for individual or group work; the two rooms include a seminar-style room and a top room with soft chairs.
cards.short_summary: Two first-come reading rooms with distinct table and soft-seating setups.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library says Firestone's two Tower Reading Rooms are first-come, first-served for individual and group study.
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served; located inside Firestone Library. Confirm building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Firestone Discovery Hub
cards.subtitle: Firestone Library
cards.notes: Use this flexible space when your work needs conversation and shared materials; it is designated for students working together.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative, flexible study setting inside Firestone.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library identifies the Firestone Discovery Hub as a collaborative, flexible student study space.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Firestone Library; confirm current building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Firestone Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Firestone Library · reservable
cards.notes: Reserve a room ahead when you need a defined group-work session, and use the booking link supplied by Princeton University Library.
cards.short_summary: Eight reservable rooms for collaborative study planning.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library states that Firestone offers eight study rooms that can be booked ahead of time.
cards.access_notes: Advance booking required; room availability and eligibility are managed through the Library reservation system.

cards.title: Lewis Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Lewis Science Library · 3rd, 4th, and A floors
cards.notes: Find an unoccupied carrel for individual work; 29 are spread across Lewis and 15 more sit in the Fine Hall Wing.
cards.short_summary: Individual carrels distributed through Lewis and the Fine Hall Wing.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library says Lewis has 29 carrels on its 3rd, 4th, and A floors plus 15 in the Fine Hall Wing, available for anyone to use.
cards.source_title: Lewis Study Carrels | Princeton University Library
cards.access_notes: Available for anyone to use; confirm current Lewis Science Library building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Lewis Treehouse
cards.subtitle: Lewis Science Library
cards.notes: Use the Treehouse for collaborative work when no event is scheduled; look for the canopied windows, clerestories, and comfortable furniture.
cards.short_summary: An event venue that becomes a student study space when unprogrammed.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library says students may use the Lewis Treehouse as study space when no events are scheduled.
cards.access_notes: Available for student study only when no event is scheduled; confirm library access and any reservation schedule first.

cards.title: Oasis
cards.subtitle: Commons Library · third floor
cards.notes: Take individual reading or laptop work to this third-floor open room, where the library specifically notes a light-filled setting.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, light-filled reading room in Commons Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library describes Oasis as a light-filled open reading room on the third floor of Commons Library.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Commons Library; confirm current building access and hours before visiting.
